This handbook does not cover all aspects, system design of hydraulic pressure equipment design common standards, public and standard materials, and also based on relevant standards and practical experience results, puts forward the technical requirements for hydraulic cylinder design and (re)manufacturing technology. The hydraulic cylinder design calculation method, hydraulic cylinder test method, and through large-scale hydraulic cylinder product research and engineering test verification (including partial test and verification), to select products with practical value for industrial application before the scene of the hydraulic cylinder design and (re)manufacturing technology.

This handbook has rich content, large information capacity, wide coverage, complete standards, strong practicality, and convenient data retrieval. It can be used by hydraulic cylinder and hydraulic machinery equipment design, design, processing, assembly, testing, inspection, on-site maintenance and maintenance personnel, and can also provide higher schools related professional teachers and students reference.

Preface

In hydraulic transmission systems, power is transmitted through pressure fluid flowing in closed circuits to control and drive mechanical equipment. The hydraulic cylinder is one of the key components of such systems. It converts hydraulic power into linear mechanical force for driving equipment. Hydraulic cylinders are composed of several operating parts, components (sub-assemblies), etc., which are arranged in a single body with the piston rod and piston forming the main working parts and working seals.

In hydraulic transmission systems and devices, in addition to oil seals, sealing rings, engineering technical personnel most commonly encounter the technical issue of hydraulic cylinder design. Compared with other hydraulic components or devices, the design and manufacture of hydraulic cylinders are relatively simple and easy, but must be truly designed and manufactured to achieve a good hydraulic cylinder. Because hydraulic cylinders are difficult to determine, and hydraulic pumps are difficult to fix, it is possible to achieve the desired effect. Moreover, hydraulic cylinders are often used as standard or small batch (quantity) production, with shared materials, heat treatment processes, process equipment, assembly, and inspection standards that are difficult to achieve. Any small mistake in design can lead to major failures. Using hydraulic cylinders as an example, if the sealing system design does not meet requirements, or if the design, processing, manufacturing, and component dimensions are not properly handled, or if internal and external leakage occurs, only replacing the sealing ring will solve the problem, which will result in great human and material waste. Currently, failures caused by thermal processing problems in the field have led to batch defects in the piston rod and piston seals, causing early fatigue fractures and leading to early wear and damage of hydraulic cylinder equipment. This is a lesson that the author has learned from each design; when conducting hydraulic cylinder design, safety, carefulness, adherence to standards, and use of proven calculation methods must be considered.

Currently, hydraulic cylinder control is relatively simple, showing that products conforming to JB/T 11718-2013 (Hydraulic Cylinder Technical Conditions) are available, as well as products conforming to GB/T 32957-2016 (Liquid and Gas Transmission System Equipment with Seamless or Welded Precision Steel Tubes) and precision seamless steel tubes, as well as products conforming to YB/T 4673-2018 (Cold-drawn Precision Seamless Steel Tubes) seamless tubes. However, the requirements for the connection and sealing of the front and rear end caps are still the main issue. If not handled properly, batch defects may result. Therefore, the manufacturing process of hydraulic cylinders is very important. According to the actual production design of hydraulic cylinders, the overall processing technology and equipment for the manufacturing process must be correctly guided to ensure product quality.

The internal leakage rate and/or external leakage rate of a hydraulic cylinder is an important indicator of its quality or performance. The hydraulic cylinder's actual use and compliance with current various hydraulic cylinder standards are largely determined by the leakage rate; at the same time, in current various hydraulic cylinder standards, most of the content is related to sealing requirements and sealing-related content. Therefore, the sealing design of hydraulic cylinders is very important.

The assembly of hydraulic cylinders is a specialized technical task. Due to the limitations of production batch sources, hydraulic cylinder assembly cannot use complete interchangeability methods, and often requires the use of group methods, adjustment methods, or matching methods. Therefore, assembly operations require not only hydraulic cylinder design and process knowledge, but also measurement technology, assembly dimensions and calculations, and assembly techniques. For this reason, this section will discuss a good hydraulic cylinder that is not only designed but also assembled.

Regardless of the hydraulic cylinder type (specification), whether it is factory (test) inspection or field testing, the test method for hydraulic cylinders must be comprehensive, accurate, and can fully demonstrate the main issues; moreover, the reliability and durability of hydraulic cylinders and their environmental adaptability should be verified through testing. This is very important for hydraulic cylinders used in aerospace and military fields. For this reason, this manual introduces the use of equipment test environment testing methods.

Hydraulic cylinders are typically only one component of a hydraulic system. The hydraulic pump (machine) is one component, and must meet the technical requirements of the hydraulic machine (machine). However, in the design and manufacture of hydraulic cylinders, it is often overlooked that hydraulic cylinders cannot meet the technical requirements of the hydraulic machine (machine), resulting in hydraulic cylinders becoming the shortest component in the hydraulic machine system. This manual.

This handbook is based on the relevant standards for hydraulic cylinders (jacks) and the experience of designing and manufacturing hydraulic cylinders (jacks), providing an overview of hydraulic cylinder design and selection, and highlighting some technical aspects of hydraulic cylinders in the relevant standards. It is intended to serve as a reference for the design and configuration of hydraulic cylinders (jacks).

Like other hydraulic components, hydraulic cylinders can only operate under certain conditions (as specified) and cannot be transported or stored under all possible conditions to ensure a certain service life. Therefore, hydraulic cylinders require proper use and regular maintenance. Among these, the selection of hydraulic fluid quality is crucial, and the use and maintenance are also important. However, the on-line inspection (monitoring) of hydraulic fluid quality does not require equipment, and at the same time, personnel must have certain practical experience.

In recent years, new standards, new materials, new structures, new processes, and new products have emerged in the field of hydraulic cylinder design and manufacturing. This handbook has timely absorbed and summarized the hierarchical technical achievements of these new standards, new designs, and new methods.

The new design philosophy and methods derived from this are a new way of thinking and method for hydraulic cylinder design, that is, in the design of new hydraulic cylinders, the remanufacturing concept should be incorporated from the beginning, making new hydraulic cylinders have the characteristics of remanufacturing. Specifically, in the design of new hydraulic cylinders, the remanufacturing properties of hydraulic cylinders and cylinder components should be evaluated in advance, and any potential problems should be corrected.

This handbook adheres to the concept of development, maintains timeliness, opens up new ideas, pursues the spirit of innovation, and strives to achieve the best combination of scientificity, advancement, applicability, and feasibility, in order to provide the fastest and most efficient hydraulic cylinders and hydraulic cylinders for the implementation of hydraulic machinery. The equipment is equipped with personnel who can independently innovate and adapt to the requirements of the national design type.
This handbook has the following characteristics:
1. Comprehensive Standards, New and Advanced

This handbook is not only comprehensive and systematic, but also draws on the standards issued and implemented before December 31, 2018, such as GB/T 35023—2018 (Hydraulic Components Evaluation Method for Sealing Performance), GB/T 36520.1—2018 (Hydraulic Drive Sealing Ring Seal Dimensions and Tolerances Part 1: Active Seal Ring Dimensions and Tolerances), GB/T 36520.2—2018 (Hydraulic Drive Sealing Ring Seal Dimensions and Tolerances Part 2: Piston Rod Seal Dimensions and Tolerances), GB/T 2348—2018 (Fluid Power Systems and Components Bore Diameter and Piston Rod Diameter), GB/T 37162.1—2018 (Hydraulic Drive Liquid Particle Size Contamination Monitoring Part 1: General), and even includes GB/T 37400.10—2019 (Heavy Machinery General Technical Specifications Part 10: Hydraulic Systems) and GB/T 37400.16—2019 (Heavy Machinery General Technical Specifications Part 16: Hydraulic Systems) standards, and based on the author's practical experience, the relevant provisions of these standards are explained.
2. Practical Content, Applicable and Reliable

This handbook includes relevant standards for hydraulic cylinder design and manufacturing, design (calculation) common formulas and materials, hydraulic cylinder and cylinder component technical requirements, etc. It provides engineers with a comprehensive, practical, and applicable reference for hydraulic cylinder design. As shown in Section 4.9, it lists seven major engineering practical machine tests (or actual test verification tests) for hydraulic cylinders as the basis for design experience. For reference by engineers in designing and manufacturing hydraulic cylinders, see Section 3.9.
3. Persist in Innovation, Pursue Progress

Innovation is the driving force for development. This handbook contains some content as a first-time publication. According to GB/T 35023—2018, the loss mode of hydraulic cylinder sealing systems is used as an example. Section 5 of this handbook is not limited to GB/T 15622—2005 (Hydraulic Cylinder Test Method) and JB/T 10205—2010 (Hydraulic Cylinder) in the specified test methods for innovation (including method selection), and also provides insights into the test methods specified in DB44/T 1169.2—2013 (Hydraulic Cylinder Part 2: Test Method) and GB/T 32216—2015 (Hydraulic Drive Proportional/Servo Controlled Pressure Cylinder Test Method), providing a comprehensive and detailed explanation of the test methods.

In addition, comparative analysis of test methods in CB/T 3812—2013 (Ship-used Hydraulic Fluid Pressure Test), JB/T 11588—2013 (Large-scale Hydraulic Oil), and GB/T 24946—2010 (Ship-used Digital Fluid Test) was conducted, and opinions were formed. During the compilation process of this handbook, support was received from many experts and professors, for which sincere thanks are expressed. Due to time constraints and the breadth of the research work, there may be omissions and inadequacies in this handbook. Readers are kindly requested to provide critical comments and corrections.
Editor

sections.text: 1.2 Hydraulic Cylinder Design and Manufacturing Standard Summary

Because standard cylinders have fixed bore and rod diameters and are suitable for general purposes, but for special requirements, non-standard cylinders can be used. This standard can be used in conjunction with other standards for non-standard cylinder design. GB/T 2348—2018 (Fluid Transmission System and Components—Cylinder and Rod Seal Dimensions), GB 2350—1980 (Fluid Gas Drive System and Components—Screw-in Cylinder Bore and Rod Diameter Series) (new standard is being formulated), etc.
1.2.1 Common Basic Standard Summary
1. GB/T 2346—2003 Hydraulic Transmission System and Components—Nominal Pressure Series Standard Summary

In fluid transmission systems, power is transmitted through the fluid (liquid or gas) flowing through the pipeline. Usually, the system and components are designed according to the fluid pressure range and pressure rating.

The standard specifies the nominal pressure series of fluid transmission systems and components. See Table 1-9. This standard applies to fluid transmission systems and components with nominal pressure ratings, and also applies to other related fluid transmission systems.

1.2.2 Scope and Normative References for Hydraulic Cylinder Product Standards

Product standards specify the requirements that products must meet to ensure their proper use. In the following standard excerpts, the scope and normative references of the standard are not specified in the document. The standards cited in the document indicate the implementation of the standard; for standards replaced by new standards, the new standard shall be used. For standards without specified dates, the use of documents shall be implemented in accordance with the latest version of the standard. For documents not specified in the date of use, the implementation of this standard shall be based on the standard, and the subsequent modifications (not including changes to the content) or revised versions that do not apply to this standard, but the agreement method of research is to use the latest version of the document. For documents not specified in the date of use, the implementation of this standard shall be based on the standard.

For example, in GB/T 241—2007, the definition of "leakage" is the test pressure under the pressure, metal substrate surface or welded seam pressure transmission interface defects; similarly, in the use of "leakage" definition of "breaking strength test", the pressure increase is measured. In GB 25974.1—2010, the definition of "external leakage" is the liquid element external leakage, with an average of 5min within the work leakage of less than one drop of leakage; in GB/T 30206.2—2013, the definition of "leakage/sealing leakage", the attached surface is normally a large amount of liquid leakage, usually due to the seal itself bearing the pressure difference, the liquid, will be in the outer surface formed into a layer of oil film, but stipulated that the inner observation does not form a drop. In JB/T 13141—2017, the definition

sections.text: referred to as 'external leakage'. When the hydraulic oil, under a certain pressure and viscosity, flows from the hydraulic cylinder's internal chamber to the atmosphere, this is called external leakage.

There is also a definition of leakage, as defined in JB/T 13566—2018, which specifies that within 10 minutes if leakage exceeds one drop of oil, it is considered leakage, not a single drop of leakage.

In reference document [102] it states: 'Leakage generally can be classified by form into: seepage, leakage, and diffusion. Leakage occurring in hydraulic cylinder seals is mainly seepage (or infiltration). Due to the characteristics of leakage classification, leakage through felt tube seals also counts as leakage, while hydraulic cylinder seal product seepage generally does not have a fixed amount. The statement that leakage occurring in hydraulic cylinder seals is primarily seepage is a classification standard.'

What also needs to be noted is that leakage (quantity) as a measure of how much leak cannot be used as leakage. Its unit can be verified through GB/Z 18427—2001, but it is not the same as leaking material. Reference document [102] states: for metal pipe fittings (full pipes or tube fittings), braze welding, and silver brazing are used. In the GB/T 241—2007 standard, 'leakage' is used within the scope of cast iron and non-ferrous metal tubes at room temperature and below, as the basic type and standard.
5. Combined Seals

In GB/T 15242.1—2017, three types of combined seals are defined along with their terminology and definitions, categorized as 'hole type combined seal', 'shaft type stepped seal', and 'shaft type sliding lip seal'. However, this standard does not provide the terminology for 'shaft seal' and 'combined shaft seal'. The standard's normative references cite GB/T 17446—2012, which also does not have the term 'combined shaft seal'. This terminology and definition has become an established convention without formal verification. For example, the term 'combined shaft seal' has become a commonly used informal term. If this is considered a problem, reference document [102] notes that in JB/T 8241—1996, the term 'shaft seal' was defined. This term 'combined shaft seal' covers the plastic seal ring combined with the rubber seal ring to form the shaft seal. Therefore, 'combined seal' also includes 'stepped seal' and 'combined shaft seal'. The term 'combined shaft seal' also includes lip seal ring cross-section surface plastic seal rings.

A combined seal (or ring) is composed of two or more of the above types of components, achieving the sealing function through different materials. The sealed components are combined into a single unit. Compared to single-material seals, the overall sealing performance of combined seals is better.

The terms 'combined shaft seal' in the context of 'combined seals' are not bore seals, but rather the distinction between combined seal types is characterized by differences. Bore seals reference bore types, while shaft seals reference shaft types. They share common features, as in the GB/T 10708.2—2000 standard, the 'ribbed rubber seal ring' and 'chevron rubber seal ring' both share these characteristics.
the characteristic that it is called 'bi-directional rubber seal ring' rather than 'combined shaft seal'.

For the definition in GB/T 15242.1—2017 regarding this type of seal, its characteristic is that the structural component is called 'plastic ring' or 'plastic part'. Therefore, see JB/T 10205—2010 regarding the definition of 'slip ring combined seal'. There is a common issue, but overall, looking at GB/T 15242.1—2017, the combined seal is better. Further analyzing 'slip ring combined seal' as a seal classification and its relationship to elastic and flexible materials, seals operate through the seal body under applied force and stress to release and achieve actual deformation, allowing the elastic deformation capability to quickly restore to its initial close fit with the sealed surface.

The above definition of 'elastic material' is derived from GB/T 15242.1—2017. The normative reference is GB/T 17446—2012, which also redefines it as 'elastic material'. The preceding description states it follows GB/T 9981—2008, while the latter states GB/T 17446—2012. The 2012 version of this standard provides normative and general rule definitions for materials and related standard specifications.
In GB/T 15242.1—2017, 'seal carrier' is defined as: the cylinder bore piston or piston rod active seal groove that relies on elastomeric force to achieve the sealed condition.
6. Sealing System
'Sealing system' is frequently found in various documents, materials, and notes. In GB/T 33217—2015 standard, it is not yet formally listed with separate terminology.

To further clarify: 'Hydraulic sealing system' refers to a given concept with an active definition. It can be referenced in document [102]. The main point is that it can be further understood by considering the design concept of hydraulic cylinder seals. Hydraulic cylinder seal design should focus on the overall sealing concept, not just individual seal components, but rather the integration of seal components with the installation groove design, unified coordination. As a general indication, if only one seal (ring) is referred to, this is the seal system terminology. However, the actual sealing characteristic is the combination of two seal component fittings, which may not necessarily be called a sealing system. For pistons with seal grooves, or two or more seal component fittings, the combined sealing system has the characteristic of increasing sealing reliability. A single seal fitting cannot be used as a sealing system alone. Hydraulic cylinder seal systems must meet the hydraulic cylinder seal (performance) requirements. Hydraulic cylinder seal systems are either static or dynamic seal systems. Hydraulic cylinder seal systems are composed of multiple seal systems. Hydraulic cylinder seal system emphasis is on (special) conditions.

1. Calculation of orifice and throttle flow rate
The calculation formula for orifice and throttle flow rate is shown in Formula 1-49.
2. Calculation of flow rate in annular throttle

For liquid flowing through an annular throttle, the flow rate calculation formula is generally calculated using liquid pressure static, dynamic seal processing flow rate calculation formula (see Formula 1-50 in Table 1-50), and in accordance with JB/T 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Tank" standard symbols and formulas.
3. Liquid jet impact calculation

In a hydraulic system, the pressure generated by the impact of a liquid jet on a component due to the sudden change in momentum can cause pressure (pressure) impact. When the pressure changes (such as starting, stopping, or changing direction), the inertia of the liquid and the elastic deformation of the pipe cause pressure changes, which can be calculated using the formula for pressure (pressure) impact calculation (see Formula 1-51).

sections.text: 3. Composite Cylinder Calculation Formula

Due to the effect of internal pressure at the thick-walled cylinder at r = r_i and r = r_e points (if the cylinder inner circle surface and outer cylindrical surface), the stress is very large, making the cylinder layer material unable to be fully utilized. To make full use of the material strength and distribute the stress more evenly, a composite cylinder structure is adopted. For composite cylinders with high internal pressure, the outer cylinder is used to reinforce the inner cylinder. The composite cylinder structure allows the outer cylinder to be pre-stressed, which can reduce the maximum stress in the inner cylinder and improve the utilization of the outer layer material, thereby increasing the load-carrying capacity of the composite cylinder and better utilizing the outer layer material.

sections.text: 5. Calculation Formula for Pressure Rod Stability

A hydraulic cylinder has at least one end that can be fixed or moved. The pressure rod (variable body) can be externally supported and its displacement relative to other components can be stable. The deformation of the variable body is stable, and the critical load value of the variable body under pressure is called the "critical buckling load".
For a cylinder with a fixed end and a free end with diameter d, when the distance between the two ends is l and l/d > 10, generally a pressure rod stability calculation (or buckling check) is required. The calculation formula is shown in 1-67.

sections.text: 1.7.3 Allowable Stress and Static Stress Calculation for Hydraulic Cylinders
1. Allowable Stress

1) Allowable stress in the hydraulic cylinder. The allowable stress in the hydraulic cylinder shall not exceed the material's allowable stress or 0.2% yield strength limit of 70% (when using cast iron, use 65% of the yield strength); the shear stress shall not exceed the material's allowable shear stress limit of 65%.
The allowable tensile stress of the hydraulic cylinder rod base shall not exceed 80% of the material's allowable stress limit.

2) Allowable stress for fixed and supported ends under fixed load. The allowable stress for fixed and supported ends under fixed load shall not exceed the material's allowable stress limit when the load is applied.
Note: This item only applies to materials with yield strength, not to hydraulic pressure.

3) Allowable stress for fixed and supported ends under variable load. Under variable load conditions, the allowable stress for fixed and supported ends shall not exceed the material's allowable stress limit (calculated stress) when the load is applied. When the load is applied in the same direction (if support is not provided), the allowable stress for fixed and supported ends under variable load shall not exceed the material's allowable stress limit.

4. Thread Marking

Complete thread marking includes the thread characteristic code, size code, tolerance band code, and pitch code. The general thread marking of metric threads is represented by the letter "M" followed by the nominal diameter in mm and the pitch in mm.
Example 1: M8×1, indicating a metric thread with nominal diameter 8 mm and pitch 1 mm of a single-start fine thread.
For multi-start threads, the pitch can be marked after the nominal diameter. Example 2: M8, indicating a metric thread with nominal diameter 8 mm and pitch 1.25 mm of a multi-start thread.

The tolerance band code includes the tolerance band code and tolerance band position code. The tolerance band position code is placed after the tolerance band code. Each nominal diameter tolerance band code is represented by the tolerance band position letter (internal thread uses uppercase letters, external thread uses lowercase letters) combined with the tolerance grade number.

If the tolerance band code and tolerance band position code are the same as the nominal diameter (internal thread is smaller than external thread), the tolerance band code is represented by a single tolerance band code followed by the nominal diameter tolerance band code. Example 3: External thread: M10×1-5g6g, indicating that the tolerance band position is 5g and the tolerance band position is 6g of the nominal diameter tolerance band. M10-6g, indicating that the tolerance band position is 6g of the nominal diameter tolerance band. Internal thread: M10×1-5H6H, indicating that the tolerance band position is 5H and the tolerance band position is 6H of the nominal diameter tolerance band.

The tolerance band code for the 6H tolerance band of the nominal diameter tolerance band is M10-6H. The tolerance band code and tolerance band position code are separated by a slash "/". Example 4: M6-6H/6g, indicating that the tolerance band position is 6H of the internal thread tolerance band and the tolerance band position is 6g of the external thread tolerance band.
M20×2-6H/5g6g, indicating that the tolerance band position is 6H of the internal thread tolerance band and the tolerance band position is 5g6g of the external thread tolerance band.

In the following cases, the tolerance band code of the internal thread with medium precision can be omitted: a) Internal thread: —5H tolerance band diameter is less than or equal to 1.4 mm; —6H tolerance band diameter is less than or equal to 1.6 mm.
b) External thread: —6h tolerance band diameter is less than or equal to 1.4 mm; —6g tolerance band diameter is less than or equal to 1.6 mm.

1.7.5 Rod-Shaped Structure Design Workmanship and Structural Requirements
1. Product Structure Workmanship Review

For newly designed products or product improvements initiated by customers, in the design process should conduct product structure workmanship review. External products should be sampled, in production before mass production should conduct product structure workmanship review. Product structure workmanship review purpose: to enable products to meet quality and user requirements, in the current production conditions can use less economical, reasonable methods to control production, and prevent problems in production.

Workmanship is used as a production tool and use of process two aspects; evaluation form is also workmanship evaluation and quantitative evaluation two types. Evaluation of product structure workmanship should consider the following factors: 1) Product category and recovery frequency. 2) Product production type. 3) Production efficiency and economy. 4) Current production, use, maintenance, recovery conditions. (1) Learning structure of castings, forgings, stamping, rolling, pressing, welding, heat treatment, cutting and matching process basic requirements 1) Learning structure of castings workmanship; a. Casting structure should meet the requirements of uniform wall thickness, balance, to meet the requirements of the situation, to avoid excessive wall thickness, to reduce control standards. b. Casting design should be reasonable, and should not have sharp angles. c. Casting structure should be quantified, to help prevent shrinkage cavities. d. Strengthen the structure and distribution management, to avoid cold junction time casting deformation or cracking. e. Casting material matching. f. Casting internal cavity structure should use less core sand, and help prevent type shrinkage and gas. 2) Learning structure of forgings workmanship; a. Structure should be simple and symmetrical. b. Template structure should be quantified, to ensure the modulus angle. c. Material and structure should have consistency. 3) Learning structure of stamping workmanship; a. Structure should be simple and symmetrical. b. External shape and hole distribution should avoid sharp angles. c. Round corner radius should be large enough to avoid deformation. d. Material selection should meet process requirements. 4) Learning structure of rolling workmanship; a. Welding structure material should have welding properties. b. Welding position should have advantages to reduce small welding stress and deformation, and help prevent material brittleness. c. Welding head shape, position and size should meet the requirements of welding material. d. Welding structure should meet the requirements of welding operation. e. Welding structure should meet the requirements of welding operation safety and reduce environmental pollution requirements. 5) Learning structure of heat treatment workmanship; a. Heat treatment process requirements should be reasonable. b. Heat treatment structure should avoid sharp angles, prevent deformation and loss. c. Surface should be uniform and symmetrical.

d. The part material should correspond to the required physical properties, and the mechanical properties should be appropriate.
e. The part material heat treatment process should prevent environmental pollution and reduce waste.
f. The structural design of the part should be conducive to processing.

a. Dimensions, tolerances, geometric tolerances and surface structure requirements should be reasonable and economical.
b. Each processing surface should have a reasonable surface roughness specification.
c. Related surface finish requirements should be specified in the first assembly drawing.

d. The structural design of the part should be conducive to multi-process simultaneous processing.
e. The structural design of the part should be systematic and enable full utilization of general equipment and standard tools for processing.

f. The part structure should facilitate multiple simultaneous processing.
g. The part structure should be conducive to assembly, processing and inspection.
h. The part structure should be conducive to using lighter cutting fluid processing.
7) Assembly Process:

items: a. Should use modular assembly when using complex assembly processes.
b. For parts weighing 20 (or 15) kg or more, the assembly unit elements should have assembly structural requirements.
c. During assembly, measures should be taken to avoid damage to intermediate disassembly and reassembly.
d. The selection method for each group component should ensure that the minimum working speed is maintained.
e. Various connection structure types should facilitate assembly and automation.

sections.text: (3) Process Audit Content
To ensure good workmanship in the design of products, process audits should be conducted at various stages of product design.
1) Initial Design Stage Audit:

items: a. Analyze design points and verify compliance with management requirements.
b. Analyze structural inheritance.
c. Analyze structural standardization, modularization, universalization, and serialization.
d. Analyze whether each component is conducive to assembly, adjustment and maintenance.
e. Analyze whether the product meets the requirements for outsourcing and processing.
f. Analyze whether material selection is reasonable.
g. Analyze the feasibility of main parts outsourcing processing.

sections.text: 2) Technical Design Stage Audit:

items: a. Analyze whether each component can be processed and inspected feasibly.
b. Analyze the feasibility of assembly configuration.
c. Analyze whether assembly configuration avoids cutting and processing of cutting fluid.

sections.text: 3) Working Drawing Design Stage Audit:

items: a. Each part should have assembly standards to facilitate assembly.
b. Each major part should be flat-assembled to facilitate assembly of sub-parts.
c. Each part should be recoverable after use for recycling and utilization.
d. Audit the structure, strictness, and welding of parts, cutting, heat treatment, special processing and assembly workmanship.

sections.text: e. Audit whether each part design process can produce harmful environmental impacts or reduce or eliminate them.

sections.text: 3. Chemical nickel-phosphorus alloy plating layer specification (from GB/T 13913—2008)

Chemical nickel-phosphorus alloy plating layer is commonly used in hydraulic cylinders. In the chemical nickel plating solution, phosphoric acid is used as a reducing agent, so that the metal can be separated without electrochemical oxidation. Since the reaction is self-catalytic, it can be carried out. Only chemical dissolution liquid with pH controlled by irregular shape of the workpiece can obtain uniform plating layer, which can reduce the accumulation of sediment.

The obtained plating layer contains at least 14% (mass fraction) of phosphorus through the bath and solution heat treatment. The chemical nickel-phosphorus structure, physical and chemical properties determine the composition of the plating layer, chemical nickel-phosphorus structure, physical and chemical properties determine the composition of the plating layer, and basic pretreatment and post-heat treatment.

Chemical nickel-phosphorus plating can effectively prevent hydrogen embrittlement and provide lubrication performance. Generally speaking, when the plating contains composite additives 8% (mass fraction) and above, the hydrogen embrittlement ability will be significantly improved; when the phosphorus content is at least 8% (mass fraction) and below, the corrosion resistance can be improved. But through appropriate heat treatment, the phosphorus content of the plating layer can be reduced to 8% (mass fraction) and below, and the corrosion resistance can be improved. However, through appropriate heat treatment, the phosphorus content of the plating layer can be reduced to 8% (mass fraction) and below, and the corrosion resistance can be improved.

(1) Corrosion resistance of chemical nickel-phosphorus plating. Thickness application conditions are shown in Table 1-133. Under different use conditions, the chemical nickel-phosphorus plating has the smallest thickness. If the plating thickness is too small, the chemical nickel-phosphorus plating will not have the best corrosion resistance. The substrate material with Ra<0.2μm should be used as a sample plate.

Due to the possible passage of controlled chemical nickel-phosphorus accumulation, the ability to meet different use requirements of chemical nickel-phosphorus plating is obtained. Therefore, engineering and technical personnel can refer to the relevant special requirements to determine the plating layer characteristics. Table 1-134 lists different use conditions below which chemical nickel-phosphorus plating types and phosphorus compound content are used.

2.1 Classification and Structure of Hydraulic Cylinders
2.1.1 Classification and Types of Hydraulic Cylinders

According to the application purpose of the project (function or use), hydraulic cylinders are classified. Hydraulic cylinders provide driving force for linear motion of machinery and equipment. Further classification of hydraulic cylinders (divided by position class) is difficult. Currently, there is one type mentioned in JB/T 10205-2010, and other standards such as JB/T 2184-2007 define seven types of hydraulic cylinders; GB/T 17446-2012 and GB/T 17446-1998 (already abolished) define 20 types of hydraulic cylinders; GB/T 9094-2006 specifies 64 types of hydraulic cylinder installation methods.

GB/T 13342-2007 specifies that commonly used marine hydraulic cylinders have the following two types: rod-type cylinders; bushing-type hydraulic cylinders and their dual-use rod-type hydraulic cylinders. However, not all hydraulic cylinders are limited to the scope defined in the standard. Hydraulic cylinders can be classified by working method, and can be single-acting and dual-acting. Single-acting cylinders are those where the fluid can act in one direction to perform work (or cushioning); dual-acting cylinders are those where the fluid can act in both directions to perform work.
In the standard (including those not covered by standards), the definitions of hydraulic cylinders in Table 2-1 have been established.

Taking the accumulator as an example, its composition includes a main accumulator (bladder), bladder, active piston, piston rod, accumulator, guide rod, sealing ring, buffer, gas charging port, transmission interface, etc. If the liquid servo accumulator is composed of active accumulator, oil block and oil pipe, etc.

The liquid element type number uses a unified format using language symbols and numbers. The servo accumulator type is divided into three parts: the upper part displays the servo accumulator name and structural characteristics, the middle part displays the servo accumulator code number, and the lower part displays the servo accumulator and other characteristic parameters.
(1) Servo Accumulator Type Internal Content

1) According to JB/T 2184–2007 regulations, the prefix (number) uses the pull-in number to represent the servo accumulator's rated pressure number. If the pull-in number is "2", it indicates the rated pressure number, with the unit being MPa.

2) According to JB/T 2184–2007 regulations, the code DC※ represents the name of the servo accumulator, and the specific meaning is the liquid servo accumulator (DC) ※ liquid accumulator (G). ※ Specific instructions refer to JB/T 2184–2007 regulations.

3) According to JB/T 2184–2007 regulations, for accumulators composed of liquid servo accumulators, the composition of combined elements should be represented by DC codes, and liquid servo accumulator codes should not be included in the nomenclature.

4) Refer to JB/T 2184–2007 regarding the definition of structural code numbers. The cylinder should use the sealing element to perform 100% sealing inspection; the cylinder should be free of oil leakage after inspection, and should reach Grade I as defined in NB/T 47013.3.

2.5 Design of Hydraulic Cylinder Seals

In GB/T 17446–2012, the design of hydraulic cylinder seals is defined. Under the action of fluid pressure, the sealing performance of the cylinder should be maintained, and the sealing should be combined with the cylinder hole (seal) seal configuration. According to the sealing situation, the seal hole (seal) is divided, and the hole will be sealed. According to JB/T 4174–2014, the seal structure is defined: the seal head and seal rod are sealed, the seal hole is sealed, and the seal hole is sealed. Compared with the above standard, the problem is not in line with JB/T 4174–2014 definition of "seal" in this handbook.
2.5.1 Structural Form

Hydraulic cylinder seals have the characteristics of high sealing degree and directional guidance (or seal length). For the welding of pressure and seal rod connections, the material has good weldability. According to the seal structure on the seal and the combined form, the seal system (seal, guide, etc.) components, time and life; seal and seal rod connection structure (including seal structure), sufficient sealing contact area, and corresponding guide structure. Hydraulic seals have two forms of structure and combined structure. The combined form is in GB 2880–1981 (Hydraulic Cylinder Seals and Seal Rings—Dimensional Series and Public Specifications) in the seal configuration. Each seal structure type is shown in Section 4.9 of the pressure cylinder design selection and reference sample. The same factory produces the same model of hydraulic cylinder seal, which must have interchangeability. The design process should ensure that the seal has free-floating properties, that is, the seal should have both fixed and optional properties.

The seal rod and seal rod are one-piece structural material, and other uses are made of common materials as follows:

2.6 Hydraulic cylinder active rod design
GB/T 17446-2012 defines the active rod as a rod that is integrated with the active rod, transmits the displacement from the piston to the mechanical and kinematic elements.
2.6.1 General principles

The hydraulic cylinder active rod should have sufficient rigidity, strength and shear strength (hardness), and should meet the requirements of the combined formula (or active rod activity rod welding), active rod, and the strength index should meet the welding quality level specified in GB/T 3323.

The active rod connection with the piston must be able to ensure the connection structure (including the locking mechanism), the sealing connection degree, and should be able to prevent disassembly (such as active rod and piston is a vibration damping).
The structural design of the active rod must be able to utilize the bending strength and rigidity.
The active rod structure design must take into account the bending strength and rigidity.

With external load on the outer surface of the active rod, it should be designed to meet the standard tolerance hand surface. When the active rod is small and the law is set to the standard flat surface situation, it can be omitted.
The welded joint of the active rod must select the connection end surface (opening type or closed type), to avoid excessive liquid pressure cylinder internal overflow.
Various active rod structural forms in Section 4.9 of the hydraulic cylinder design and selection should be referred to.
The same batch of hydraulic cylinders produced by the same manufacturer must have interchangeability.
Design should consider the durability of the active rod and the durability of the seal.
2.6.2 Structural form

The active rod axis is integrated with the active rod, without active rod separation. However, in practical applications, there are open-end bottom openings, which form a seamless structure without rod discharge accumulation.

sections.text: The most damaging to the inner wall of the cylinder is friction corrosion. In theory, it is possible to affect the pressure holding ability, pressure (elastic) stiffness, (friction) damping or other characteristics. If the pressure drops during operation, the liquid film thickness decreases, and when the pressure drops, the elastic deformation of the accumulated liquid film decreases, which may also cause vibration of the liquid column and the piston rod.

The piston rod in the cylinder is usually equipped with a guide, which limits the lateral movement of the piston rod and prevents the piston rod from being in contact with the cylinder wall. This guide can be used as a piston rod guide, which can prevent the piston rod from being in the guide design to reduce friction (rod) return speed, to avoid excessive impact on the bottom.

The piston rod and piston rod connection with the belt and rope groove piston rod, because the piston rod groove is designed to be able to transmit the signal from the piston rod to the piston rod return operation. According to the piston rod design, it can be used in GB 2350-1980 (Hydraulic Transmission System Components Piston Rod Groove Type and Size Series) standards, the thread pitch can be shortened.

The dynamic surface of the piston rod is hardened, the hardened layer depth (measured from the surface, polished or ground) is generally within the range of 0.03–0.05 mm; the hardened layer hardness is 800–1000 HV; the hardened layer must have a bright polished surface, and the hardened layer must not have edge lifting; during the design of the maximum load and/or variable load, the hardened layer must not have edge lifting. When the cylinder is working, the active sample should be exposed to a part of the hardened layer.

Except for the hardened layer, the active sample outer surface can also use chemical hardening.

If special requirements are needed for the sample surface, the spray coating composite gold or spray ceramic coating can be used.

GB/T 32217–2015 stipulates that the test sample should have a residual stress after hardening of 0.015–0.03 mm thick hardened layer.

The hydraulic cylinder anti-adhesion, zinc coating or other required coatings should be applied to the piston rod technical requirements. The coating should meet the standards and requirements specified in the relevant standards and should be verified (measured).

For equipment without hardened piston rods, the hardened layer coating on the active sample surface should be consistent, without obvious defects, no scratches, no cracks, no spots, no waves, no flaking, no corrosion, no hair, no burrs, no cracks, no pits, no rust, no oxidation and other defects.

The inspection should be carried out under good lighting conditions under a magnifying glass of 3–5 times, and must be able to use 3–5 times magnification to check.

The sealing groove structure on the piston rod, in addition to the sealing groove shown in the working drawing, should be consistent.

The hydraulic cylinder bottom should meet the strength, rigidity and impact resistance requirements (cylinder). It must be welded to the cylinder body (cylinder), and the welding quality must meet the strength index of GB/T 3323 Class II.

2.8.2 Structural Types

According to the installation type of the hydraulic cylinder, the cylinder and rear flange are fixed together (double) ring, circular (square, rectangular) shape and other forms to form an integrated structure.

The cylinder bottom liquid inlet and outlet openings are located at different positions, dividing the axial oil passage and radial oil passage. The cylinder bottom and cylinder (cylinder) connection type adopts flange connection, internal (external) screw connection, pull pin connection, welding, etc. Among them, the cylinder bottom and cylinder (cylinder) adopt welded connection as the normal fixed (fixed) type, that is, the cylinder bottom is welded to the cylinder body.

The cylinder bottom structure type is generally a closed type (cylinder) or open type (cylinder). The end face of the cylinder bottom is generally hemispherical, and the cylinder bottom (center) has an axial oil hole (hole) or a valve hole for the cylinder bottom called a hole cylinder bottom.

2.8.8 Strength Calculation of Cylinders

It is necessary to perform strength and rigidity calculations. The most ideal shape of the cylinder body is to use a flat-bottomed cylinder, and the non-flat bottom, with the cylinder center generally open and connected to the oil hole (or filled with safe oil hole through hole), due to the uneven stress distribution and strength calculation, it is now generally considered that there is no simple and convenient formula for calculating cylinder strength. The reason is that the stress distribution is complex and difficult to determine. It is necessary to use the formula for guiding strength calculation proposed by Soviet engineer Mixeev (B.A. Mixeev):
σd = 0.75 PR²/δ² ≤ [σ]

Where: σd—calculated stress, unit in MPa; p—liquid cylinder test pressure, unit in MPa; R—cylinder (inner) radius, unit in mm; δ—cylinder wall thickness, unit in mm; φ—coefficient, related to the ratio of bottom oil hole radius R, namely φ = (R-R)/R;
[σ]—material allowable stress, [σ] = σs/ns, safety factor ns ≥ 4-4.5.
In addition, Soviet engineer Rozanov (B.B. Розанов) proposed the strength calculation formula:
σd = PR²/φδ² ≤ [σ]
Where: φ—coefficient, taken as 0.7-0.8.
German scholar (EMuller) proposed the strength calculation formula:
σd = 0.68 PR²/δ² ≤ [σ]

The above two formulas are based on the assumption that the stress is uniformly distributed around the circumference of the flat-bottomed cylinder, and the influence of the oil hole on the stress distribution is not considered. 2.10 Hydraulic Cylinder Seal Design
2.10.1 Hydraulic Cylinder Seal Overview
1. Leakage and Sealing

Hydraulic cylinder is a kind of closed high-pressure container, relying on sealing installed in the cylinder without piston rod/or with piston rod (with active type or active rod dual use pressure cylinder for example) of the pressure work gap between the piston and liquid cylinder (rod) to prevent liquid leakage (rod) and to prevent liquid cylinder (rod) operation, mechanical function. Liquid work gap quality is affected by, sometimes pressure is greater than this is also a sign of pressure cylinder H8/f7 pressure.

Generally speaking, hydraulic work gap pressure is higher, leakage is serious, but liquid pressure work gap pressure is lower (0~2.5MPa), medium pressure (2.5~8.0MPa) should not be ignored. In practice, the pressure encountered by liquid cylinder is high pressure (16~32MPa) or higher pressure (≥32MPa) when leakage, in the middle pressure leakage.

Hydraulic cylinder leakage is refers to pressure work gap quality through the gap by, by high pressure side to low pressure side, leakage is generally divided into internal leakage, such as liquid cylinder rod liquid pressure work gap direction rod leakage, or with piston rod liquid work gap direction rod leakage, this is called internal leakage (internal); internal liquid pressure surrounding environment leakage pressure work gap direction rod leakage, such as liquid cylinder rod liquid pressure work gap direction rod leakage, or with piston rod liquid work gap direction rod leakage, this is called external leakage (external); external liquid pressure surrounding environment leakage pressure work gap direction rod leakage, such as GB/T 17446—2012 defined leakage as not having pressure and not causing volume loss of related volume flow loss.

movement. Internal leakage is defined as leakage within the cavity of a component, and external leakage is defined as leakage from a component or fitting to the external environment surrounding the pipeline. The main reasons for hydraulic cylinder leakage are: first, the mating surfaces of mating parts have gaps at the joint surfaces; second, there is a pressure difference (pressure drop) across the sealing surfaces, which affects the efficiency of the hydraulic cylinder, the speed and rate of cylinder advancement, and/or output force, etc. It also causes the hydraulic working medium to further heat up, which may lead to safety accidents; external leakage causes environmental pollution, causes work stoppages, and may cause fire hazards, etc. Therefore, whether it is leakage or external leakage, it may be a serious problem that must be taken seriously. Internal leakage (clearance) and external leakage (clearance) are mandatory inspection items for hydraulic cylinder factory testing, with specific reference to JB/T 10205-2010 and GB/T 15622-2005 standards. Hydraulic cylinder leakage is mainly collar (penetration, string) leakage.

Being able to prevent or reduce leakage of equipment is generally referred to as sealing or sealing devices. Sealing devices are composed of one or more sealing components and related structural components (such as grooves, metal rings, etc.) combined to form the assembly. Sealing devices commonly used to prevent leakage and/or prevent contaminants from entering components include: guides (supports), wipers, dust seals (Y-type, V-type supports), and anti-fouling seals collectively referred to as sealing components (some are called MT/T seals). The function of sealing is to seal the joint surfaces of two coupled surfaces, cut off the leakage channel or increase the leakage channel resistance. The main performance indicators measuring the sealing effect of a seal are: leakage rate (leakage amount/time or leakage amount/distance), applicable friction and wear characteristics, service life and applicable working conditions (pressure, speed, temperature, etc.). Currently, in China, the hydraulic seal design standards and levels, as well as processing technology and equipment, seal component structural types and parameters, sealing materials (rubber and plastic materials), additives and testing, etc. all have made relatively great progress. The sealing performance of hydraulic cylinders also has relatively great improvement. In summary, hydraulic cylinder pressure, speed, temperature, product quality improvements, service life extension, and reliability and other technical performance can to a large extent depend on the hydraulic cylinder sealing device (system) and its design.

The above-mentioned sealing is to prevent or reduce leakage measures (actions or methods). This is a concept that also means "sealing" is called "leakage seal." In addition, there are representations of leakage of this kind of phenomenon or state, which is the opposite of another concept called "leakage seal."

2. Classification of Seals

Seals are divided into static seals and dynamic seals. Static seals are for sealing components (assemblies, fittings) that have no relative motion; dynamic seals are for sealing components (assemblies, fittings) that have relative motion. This type of seal is in a relatively static working state. For the requirements of static seals, dynamic seals must not only ensure sealing force in addition to withstanding the operating pressure, but must also consider the friction, wear, and heat generated by relative movement of the contact area; ensuring a certain level of sealing performance while also ensuring that the movement performance meets the requirements, but because of the requirements for movement components' support and orientation, according to whether the sealed coupling surface is sliding or rotating motion, dynamic seals are further divided into dynamic seals and rotary seals. Dynamic seals in hydraulic cylinders include the piston (and its related) rod, piston, guide sleeve and piston rod direction seal combinations. According to the contact relationship between dynamic seals and mating seal surfaces, reciprocating seals can also be divided into contact seals and non-contact seals. Reciprocating motion dynamic seals can be further called piston seals (or called piston, rod seals) and piston rod seals (or called shaft seals, inner diameter seals). Static seals can be divided into flat static seals (end face seals) and cylindrical static seals (radial seals, inner and outer diameter static seals). Axial static seals also have both axial static seals and radial seals (see Figure 2-6a, b below). Cylindrical static seals (radial static seals)

According to the shape and sealing method of sealing parts, seals can be classified into static seals (static seals and rubber seals, strip seals, and material seals) and dynamic seals (O-ring rubber seals, Y-ring rubber seals, etc.). The structure is simple and easy to process, and the sealing effect is good. The sealing parts are installed in the seal groove and then the matching parts are assembled. The sealing parts pass through the elastic deformation of the seal to produce a certain preload. When the sealing parts receive the sealing working surface pressure, the sealing parts undergo a step change in shape, and the contact pressure (reaction force) increases, so that the sealing work can adapt to the pressure change of the sealed medium. Pressure relief type seals are a kind of contact seal. If the sealing surface (line) contact pressure increases, the friction is small, and the starting pressure is low, making the seal easy to use. However, the seal performance is not stable.

The contact seal is installed in the seal groove in the seal device and has two main functions: auxiliary seal and main seal. The auxiliary seal function is to protect the main seal and prevent the main seal from being damaged. The main seal function is to prevent leakage. If the seal is damaged, such as a circle, a block, a groove, or a groove, it will be damaged. In addition, seals can be sealed to the sealing work quality, seal material, and the unequal distribution of the sealing work surface pressure.

sections.text: Sealing systems with working pressure seals are the most common in sealed devices. However, because the unit is a single seal, if using live seals this may require consideration of the direction of the seal, and if installed incorrectly, the seal may not function properly. At times it is difficult to ensure that the structure is assembled correctly (flush). The characteristic of Y-ring is that the sealing effect is better than single seals, and it can achieve single-direction sealing by using slightly different working conditions. When the reciprocating speed is 0.5m/s, the gap is 0.2mm, the working pressure range is 0~15MPa, the gap is 0.1mm, the working pressure range is 0~20MPa. When the reciprocating speed is 0.15m/s, the gap is 0.2mm, the working pressure range is 0~20MPa, the oil pressure is 0.1mm, the working pressure range is 0~25MPa. Generally, Y-ring seals made of nitrile rubber, polyurethane rubber, and fluorine rubber are used. These three types of Y-ring seals have a temperature range of -20~80°C for use.

Regarding Y-rings, it is necessary to install support rings to prevent extrusion. According to GB/T 10708.1—2000, the medium pressure Y-ring seals are divided into groups. When the pressure wave is large, the gap of the Y-ring seal needs to be used with support rings, and if the pressure is not large, the Y-ring does not need to use support rings. When the working pressure is 14~31.5MPa, use nitrile rubber Y-ring seals; when the working pressure is 31.5~70MPa, support rings must be used. When using Y-rings with support rings, there is no friction loss, but when using Y-rings without support rings, the actual effect is very good.

2) Yx rubber seals. Yx-type rubber seals (hereinafter referred to as Yx rings) are also a type of shaped rubber seal. They are divided into two types: with holes and without holes. According to the standards JB/ZQ 4265—2006 (Yx-type rubber seals) and JB/ZQ 4264—2006 (Yx-type rubber seals), the structure of Yx rings is different from Y-rings. The sealing groove dimensions and limits of Yx rings are specified in the standard. Yx rings have a temperature range of -20~80°C and a working pressure of ≤31.5MPa under the condition of use. The surface roughness of Yx rings is 1 times higher than that of Y-rings, making it difficult to use in high-speed reciprocating conditions, which requires the addition of support rings. When the working pressure is >10MPa and the reciprocating speed is large, support rings can be used to seal the support surface to prevent one-way sealing. According to the reference document GB/T 2879—2005, the sealing groove composition of Yx rings is specified for use, which is not accurate.

3) Single Y×D seal ring and single Y×d seal ring. According to GB/T 36520.1—2018 and GB/T 36520.2—2018, the single body Y×d seal ring and the single body Y×d seal ring are both shaped nitrile rubber seals. The reciprocating speed is 0.5m/s, the maximum working pressure is 35MPa, and the working temperature range is -40~80°C, with mineral oil as the working medium.

4) V-ring rubber seal ring. V-ring rubber seal ring (hereinafter referred to as V-ring) is a shaped rubber seal ring. According to GB/T 17446—2012, the standard specifies that V-ring seals are used. The characteristics are that the rubber and leather are good, and the pressure can be large without heavy load. However, the friction is large, the resistance is large, and it must be used with a gap (flush) type seal ring. Generally, the sealing groove width is small, and in the liquid tank, the main use is live seals (active seals), and the sealing effect is good. In addition, the V-ring can also be used for static sealing. The V-ring is less resistant to use, and it is often used with rubber or rubber-plastic composite seals, called V-ring composite seals. In specific applications, 1~6 V-rings can be added together to form a V-ring composite seal, which is composed of one or more seals with a certain gap. This way, a V-ring composite seal can work at a pressure of 60MPa or higher. The working pressure of V-rings is generally 31.5MPa, and the clamping V-ring can reach 60MPa or higher; the working temperature range is -30~100°C or higher.

5) U-ring rubber seal ring. U-ring rubber seal ring (hereinafter referred to as U-ring) is a pressure-resistant seal ring used in the highest pressure sealing. According to the standard, it is a type of rubber seal ring. The live seals or active rod seals are both good sealing effects. In 2018, on July 13, the current seal ring standards in the country included U-rings, which are only in GB/T 5719—2006, with one U-ring definition, and the outer seal ring control is the product sample in the standard. U-rings and Y-rings are the same, with equal rubber and unequal pressure, and can be used for static seals, can also be used for dynamic seals, and cannot be higher than U-ring static seals. To improve the sealing effect of U-rings, reduce friction, and improve the service life, there is a type of so-called U-ring (recognized as a dual U-ring). To improve the anti-extrusion ability of U-rings, there is a U-ring with a backing ring on the bottom of the U-ring, with a U-ring, so that the elastic body (rubber) is composed of another type of U-ring. This type of U-ring seal has low temperature, low working temperature, good anti-extrusion ability, high pressure resistance, and stable high-pressure sealing performance. This handbook uses the typical U-ring, or the so-called (pre) reinforced U-ring.
According to GB/T 36520.1—2018 and GB/T 36520.2—2018 standards, single U-ring seals are provided.

2.10.2  General Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinder Seals
1. Overview

The definition of hydraulic cylinder seal is to refer to the hydraulic cylinder seal device, which is composed of the main sealing components of the hydraulic cylinder, used for sealing all moving parts (dynamic seals) and static seals (static seals). The hydraulic cylinder seal includes: active rod seals, rod seals, oil port seals, etc. The hydraulic cylinder seal device is usually also equipped with active rod dust (seals) and active seals.

Active rod guidance and support. The hydraulic cylinder seal is another definition is the relative hydraulic cylinder leakage prevention, with the same and leakage phenomenon or static state relative to another definition. The hydraulic cylinder leakage is the hydraulic work quality exceeds the allowable leakage boundary, due to high-side low-pressure leakage flow phenomenon. Leakage is divided into internal and external leakage.

In the current hydraulic cylinder standards, the hydraulic cylinder seal technology requirements are its important component, the hydraulic cylinder design and manufacturing must meet these requirements.

sections.text: 6. Compression Permanent Deformation of Rubber

When rubber is in a compressed state, physical and chemical changes will occur. When the compression force is lost, these changes will prevent the rubber from returning to its original state, resulting in permanent deformation. The magnitude of permanent deformation depends on the degree of compression and time. At room temperature, chemical vulcanization is the main cause of permanent compression deformation. At low temperatures, the main cause is the loss of elasticity. To prevent the addition of plasticizers to the sample, the pressure must be maintained at the standard temperature. At low temperatures, the glass transition temperature must be below the high temperature after recovery. In the low temperature test, the glass transition and vulcanization of the sample are the main causes.
In GB/T 7759, the test temperature is divided into room temperature and high temperature test methods.
(1) Room Temperature Compression Test Method

Under standard laboratory conditions, place the sample on the fixture at the specified compression rate. Under standard laboratory conditions, apply pressure for a specified time, then remove the pressure and place the sample in a free state. Measure the thickness of the sample at specified intervals. The measurement can be done at intervals (up to one test cycle at the highest point of the time curve). The pressure deformation can also be measured at the specified time after removal.
(2) Low Temperature Compression Test Method

Under standard laboratory conditions, place the sample on the fixture at the specified compression rate. Under the specified low temperature test conditions, maintain a constant temperature for a specified time, then remove the sample from the low temperature environment and place it in a free state at room temperature. Measure the thickness of the sample at specified intervals. The measurement can be done at intervals (up to one test cycle at the highest point of the time curve). The pressure deformation can also be measured at the specified time after removal.
Test temperature is set to (23±2)°C or (27±2)°C.
In GB/T 5720—2008 (O-ring rubber seal test method), the normative reference document uses GB/T 7759—1996 standard.
In MT/T 985, the normative reference document uses GB/T 7759—1996 standard. In MT/T 985, the permanent compression deformation of the seal at high temperature is specified:

sections.text: 7. Liquid Absorption Properties
The effect of vulcanized rubber or thermoplastic rubber on the use of hydraulic fluid is mainly manifested in the following results:

items: Liquid absorption by rubber.

sections.text: Generally, absorption (absorption capacity) causes the rubber to swell, which is called "swelling". This phenomenon causes the seal to increase in size, increase in strength, increase in hardness and other physical and chemical properties to change. In addition, due to the increase in rubber volume, the friction force increases and the aging resistance decreases. The rubber becomes brittle after soaking, and the performance after soaking is very important.

In GB/T 1690—2010 (Vulcanized rubber and thermoplastic rubber - Determination of liquid absorption) specifies that the liquid absorption test method is determined by immersing the sample in the test liquid before and after the property change, and evaluating the liquid absorption effect on the rubber.

In GB/T 5720—2008 (O-ring rubber seal test method), the normative reference document uses GB/T 1690—1992 (now replaced by GB/T 1690—2010) standard. In GB/T 5720, the quality change rate and volume change rate calculation method are specified.

Sealing pressure is the sealing ring in the working process of the pressure received by the sealing interface. sections.text: 4. Measurement Methods and Instruments
(1) Leakage

Each test sample before testing should be calibrated with a measuring cylinder of 10mL, with an accuracy of 0.1mL of the measuring cup. If the test leakage is less than 10mL, the measuring cylinder with a precision of 1mL should be used for measurement.
(2) Friction Force

1) Measurement of friction force. The friction force sensor should be installed in the test device, with the sensor mounted on the test fixture. The friction force sensor should be connected to a suitable measuring device with a recorded value on the drawing to ensure the friction force is recorded. The drawing should record the friction force value at the appropriate frequency, and the friction force vibration amplitude should be determined.
2) Measurement of dynamic friction force.
① Each test begins, and the dynamic support force should prevent the seal from being damaged by the friction force F₁.
② From the table recorded curve (see GB/T 32217-2015 Figure 2-9 and Figure 2-10), calculate the average friction force of the test seal.
See formula (2-56)
F_s = (F_i - F_t) / 4
Formula (2-56)
In the formula: F_i—the average friction force in the forward and return stroke of a single test seal;
F_t—the friction force in the forward and return stroke of the test device;
F_s—the sum of the friction force in the forward and return stroke of the test seal and test device.
Note: F_s is the average value, not the friction force of a single seal part.
3) Measurement of starting friction force.
① Set the test return path force, and perform static test during the period (such as 16h).

1) Pressure gauge. Install a pressure gauge suitable for the test, and record the test pressure on the gauge. Pressure measurement should ensure that the pressure is maintained at ±0.5% (below).

sections.text: 2.10.5  Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing Components and Their Grooves
1. O Ring Sealing Groove and Its Groove
(1) O Ring Characteristics and Function

As shown in Figure 2-17, the O ring rubber sealing ring (also called O ring) is a ring-shaped seal with a circular cross-section (or sometimes elliptical or O-shaped). It is the most commonly used seal in hydraulic systems. It can be used for static sealing and can also be used for dynamic sealing. It is now widely used in O ring sealing grooves in hydraulic systems. Generally, the hydraulic system uses O ring seals as the working seal groove.

I, II classes, each class has hardness and four sub-levels. Class I working temperature range is 40-100°C, Class II working temperature range is -25-125°C. The working fluid used is oil-based liquid and anti-wear hydraulic oil. If the working temperature is lower than the specified working conditions and working temperature, you need to select other suitable rubber materials. You can also use the groove model shown in Figure 0 to determine the groove size, measure the diameter and length of the O ring; this is just to re-design the sealing groove, or re-design the model to match the standard groove for the O ring. Due to the O ring being composed of rubber material design, the design is limited to a single unit, so there are many special cases to choose the O ring sealing groove. This design of the O ring sealing groove is more complex.
Regarding O ring design and manufacturing, readers are advised to further refer to reference [102] and other related documents.
O ring and its other sealing groove advantages:

items: Small sealing groove size
Can be double sealed, can be used manually, static sealed
Static seal performance is good
Small friction force, also suitable for high pressure exchange occasions
O ring and sealing groove are both standard, easy to select and use
Easy to assemble, low cost

(2) O Ring Sealing Design

After the O ring is determined, the O ring pressure level and expansion and contraction and work conditions are determined by the groove (or called sealing groove) design. In summary, O ring sealing groove design is a complex technical problem.
Seal groove design should meet the following requirements: reasonable groove size, easy processing and storage, precision guarantee, and convenient installation and maintenance.

GB/T 3452.3-2005 Hydraulic Cylinder O-Ring Seal Groove Standard specifies the groove dimensions and tolerances. The groove dimensions should be designed reasonably, with good machinability and precision retention. 5. V-shaped rubber sealing ring and its groove
(1) V-shaped rubber sealing ring sealing principle

The V-shaped rubber sealing ring is a type of lip-shaped sealing ring. Its cross-section is V-shaped (or its cross-section is roughly V-shaped) (hereinafter referred to as V-ring), as shown in Figure 2-28. V-shaped rubber sealing rings cannot be used alone. They must be pressed together with support rings (or elastic sealing rings) to form a set of sealing units. The sealing unit cannot be used alone. The sealing unit is composed of a V-ring, a support ring at 60°, and a pressure ring and support ring at 60°, or a larger point. The V-shaped sealing ring is used as an example. The V-ring is in a static state when the ring diameter is smaller than the sealing groove inner diameter. The V-ring inner diameter is smaller than the sealing groove inner diameter. The three-piece assembly is installed in the sealing groove. The V-ring will produce initial deformation. Due to the selection of the V-ring, this deformation occurs at the V-ring opening, and at the contact part with the support ring, the pressure is applied. When the pressure in the sealed cavity increases, the upper part of the V-ring changes contact shape, and the lip position and contact surface increase. The contact shape increases with the increase in pressure, and the sealing effect is improved. This is the "self-sealing" function. When the pressure in the sealed cavity increases, the upper part of the V-ring changes contact shape, and the lip position and contact surface increase.

(2) Sealing principle of U-ring

As shown in Figures 2-34 and 2-35, because the U-ring has a pair of sealing lips and a sealing groove, the sealing force is generated by the fluid pressure acting on the sealing lip and the elastic force of the seal material itself, forming a seal.

When the U-ring is configured, its sealing groove is matched with the mating surface U-shape diameter to the pressure, and the mating surface is tangent to the initial sealing force. The sealing lip is pressed against the mating surface, and the friction force increases with the pressure difference. The sealing lip is tangent to the sealing surface, and as the working pressure increases, the sealing force increases, and the sealing contact area increases. Therefore, the U-ring is a kind of seal with sealing function (ability) of the seal ring.

The classical U-ring is compared with the U-ring piston rod seal, and the initial sealing force is weak. Since the sealing lip is not suitable for static sealing, the sealing force is weak. The non-ring type U-ring has better internal pressure resistance, effectively overcoming the upper defects of the U-ring, making the U-ring have a pair of sealing lips comparable to the initial sealing force. Therefore, it can be used for static sealing.

The non-ring type U-ring seal is a classical U-ring because the U-ring internal cavity has U-shaped or annular recessed shape metal spring (commonly used as stainless steel), its static and dynamic sealing performance is good, can be used for rotating sealing. Due to the fact that it is in a relatively narrow working temperature range, the metal spring is hardened into an O-ring shape, and then installed into the U-ring of the U-ring groove, combined into a kind of seal that does not affect the sealing performance of the initial sealing force, and has good initial sealing force of the classical U-ring.

Another classical U-ring because the U-ring internal cavity has U-shaped or annular recessed metal spring (commonly used as stainless steel), its static and dynamic sealing performance is good, can be used for rotating sealing. Due to the fact that it is in a relatively narrow working temperature range, the metal spring is hardened into an O-ring shape, and then installed into the U-ring of the U-ring groove, combined into a kind of seal that does not affect the sealing performance of the initial sealing force, and has good initial sealing force of the classical U-ring. The U-ring material can be selected with open elements, such as force switches. This kind of U-ring material can be used for open elements.

9. Radial Seal Components and Their Grooves
(1) Common Features of Radial Seal Grooves

In JB/T 8241—1996 "Radial Seal Groove Specification", the radial seal groove is defined as: a groove machined in the shaft or hole to accommodate the seal and prevent leakage. Radial seals are generally the least one seal ring (called plastic ring, slip ring) and one elastic body composed, generally slip ring material is made of cast iron or bronze (or bimetallic copper) or hard anodized aluminum alloy, elastic body is made of rubber material control, per GB/T 15322—2017 "Radial Seal Groove and Hole Groove Specification". Radial seal grooves are divided into: O-ring grooves for circular seals; rectangular grooves for rectangular seals; trapezoidal grooves for trapezoidal seals; and combined grooves for combined seals composed of multiple seal rings.

Radial seal components are used for hydraulic oil as the working medium, with working pressure ≤40 MPa, in reciprocating motion speed ≤5m/s, working temperature range -40~200°C. After many years of development and technological advancement, working pressure can reach 60 MPa, in reciprocating motion speed can be 15m/s, but the working temperature range has no major changes, mainly because the elastic body (referring to the O-ring material) has limited temperature range. It is necessary to clarify that not all O-ring materials are suitable for -40~200°C working temperature range, but only for low temperature use.
Special properties of radial seal components are described in Section 2.10.5.14.
(2) Radial Seal Components and Their Dual-Use and Working Characteristics

Radial seal components are generally composed of two groups, with the elastic body commonly seen as O-ring rubber seal ring, also available as (short) shaped mountain rubber seal ring; slip ring surface is mostly multi-sample, with shaped material and smooth slip ring commonly used. Radial seal components are not only used for active and static sealing, but also for use in dry sealing.

10. Several Non-standard Seal Types and Their Grooves
(1) Rod Seal with Active Rod Seal Combination Seal Groove

The active rod seal combination seal groove (hereinafter referred to as the active rod seal combination groove) is a seal groove composed of two types of materials separately manufactured and assembled together.

As shown in Figure 2-51, the active rod seal combination is a shaped seal, with the seal groove made of nitrile rubber (93HA), with a groove shape approximately three-shaped, and the rod is made of material, with higher hardness than the seal groove.
The main key points are:

items: Good wear resistance.
